solutions.latex: Stationary points occur when $f'(x)=0$: $3x^2-k=0$. At $x=-1$: $3(-1)^2-k=0$, so $k=3$.

$y$-intercept: $f(0)=1$, i.e. $(0,1)$.

$f'(x)=x^3-4x=x(x^2-4)=0\Rightarrow x=0,\ \pm2$, giving $(0,1)$, $(2,-3)$, $(-2,-3)$.

$f''(x)=3x^2-4$. $f''(0)=-4<0$, so $(0,1)$ is a local maximum. $f''(\pm2)=8>0$, so $(2,-3)$ and $(-2,-3)$ are local minima.

Possible inflection: $f''(x)=0\Rightarrow x=\pm\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}\approx\pm1.15$. Concavity changes at both, so $\left(\pm\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3},-\dfrac{11}{9}\right)$ are points of inflection. The curve is concave down for $-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}<x<\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}$.

End points: $f(\pm3)=3.25$, i.e. $(\pm3,3.25)$.
